text:
Elaine: Heads up — opened a docs PR for Dedicated autoscale examples + SLA wording tweaks. Need a quick review before EOD. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1722
Samir: On it. Which sections changed — provisioning, autoscale policy, or SLA table?
Elaine: Autoscale policy section + reserved pools note about preemption/isolation. I added a minimal YAML example and a Python SDK snippet. Also tightened wording in the SLA paragraph to clarify the 99.9% target applies to the Dedicated control plane + route fallback behavior.
Lena: I can skim the YAML/SDK. Paste the snippets here so I can comment inline. Quick wins to watch for: burst example, eviction priority, and explicit min_replicas.
Elaine: YAML below (added comments):
```yaml
apiVersion: rwinference/v1
kind: ReservedPool
metadata:
  name: team-embedding-pool
spec:
  reserved_capacity_type: on-demand   # use on-demand for stricter SLA guarantees
  autoscale:
    min_replicas: 2
    max_replicas: 20
    target_concurrency_per_gpu: 8
    burst_policy:
      enabled: true
      max_burst_replicas: 4
  isolation:
    eviction_priority: best-effort  # prefer moving/evicting best-effort tenants
```
Elaine: Python SDK snippet I added:
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient()
pool = client.create_reserved_pool(name="team-embedding-pool", config={
    "capacity_type": "on-demand",
    "autoscale": {"min": 2, "max": 20, "target_concurrency": 8},
    "burst": {"enabled": True, "max_replicas": 4}
})
print(pool.id)
```
Chris: LGTM on structure, but the YAML uses `preemptible: true` in one comment earlier — we don't expose that flag in the provisioning API. Suggest keeping examples to fields we actually support (e.g., `reserved_capacity_type`). Also change `eviction_priority` values to match the enum we document (e.g., `best-effort`/`protected`).
Samir: Good catch. Also add an explicit note about tenant isolation — Reserved pools are isolated logically but if customers use spot-backed hosts they can see host-level preemption. Recommend the docs say: "For strict SLA, choose reserved_capacity_type: on-demand and avoid spot-backed hosts."
Elaine: Updated the PR with those changes and fixed the SLA matrix link (was pointing to old /handbook URL). @DocsBot can you re-run lint?
DocsBot: Lint checks passed — 2 warnings: YAML comment line length (non-blocking).
Lena: :thumbsup: I'll add a tiny follow-up to include an autoscale simulator note. Also we should add a short "Migration hints" bullet for teams moving from Hosted -> Dedicated. Common pitfall: cache warming and KV cache TTLs cause cold-start latency spikes.
Chris: Add this to the migration checklist: "warm caches, conservative autoscale min_replicas, test rollbacks, monitor per-route latency for 72h, and validate token/key rotation."
Elaine: Good list. I'll push one more commit to include that checklist and a short example command to warm caches.
Samir: One nit: rephrase the SLA paragraph to avoid implying we guarantee per-tenant latency — we guarantee control-plane availability and offer policy fallbacks. After that, approve.
Lena: Approved. I left two tiny suggestions inline (wording/terminology).
Samir: Approved.
Elaine: Merged — thanks everyone! :party_parrot:
DeployBot: Docs site build queued for the PR merge; preview URL will be posted when ready.
Chris: Nice — can someone add a quick link from "Dedicated Quickstart" -> "Migration checklist" so customers find it?
Elaine: Added a follow-up issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/431 — will assign in the morning.
Lena: Thanks, that should close the loop.
Elaine: Closing thread — will follow up if build preview shows any rendering issues.
